results.title: IMF raises Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% on chip boom
results.content: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday upgraded its growth forecast for the South Korean economy to 3.9 percent for this year, up 0.6 percentage point from its earlier projection last month, amid the accelerating global semiconductor supercycle. An IMF delegation, led by mission chief Corinne Delechat, made the forecast after a two-week consultation with key Korean economic and financial institutions, including the Ministry of Finance and Economy. The IMF's World Economic Outlook earlier projected 3.3 percent growth. The team also said the Korean economy will grow 3.3 percent in 2027, marking growth of more than 3 percent for the second consecutive year. "The global AI upcycle is providing an exceptional boost to the Korean economy through record-high semiconductor exports, driving strong corporate earnings and fiscal revenue," it said. However, even though I am far from being a hallyu expert, I am frequently asked to explain the factors behind the success of Korea's cultural industries. I usually wave off the question, insisting that I am not qualified to speak on the subject. Nevertheless, people often press me to share my own perspective on how Korea's cultural sector developed and achieved such remarkable global popularity. results.title: Upstage, Cohere build AI tailored for national data control
results.content: Korean artificial intelligence (AI) startup Upstage has joined forces with Canadian company Cohere to develop sovereign AI — systems built and controlled locally to keep sensitive data and infrastructure independent of foreign tech giants — as they pursue enterprise customers in Korea and overseas. Upstage said Tuesday it had signed a strategic partnership with Cohere, which specializes in sovereign AI for regulated industries and government agencies. The agreement brings together Upstage's proprietary large language models, Solar Pro and Solar Mini, and its document-processing technology, Document Parse, with Cohere's enterprise agentic AI platform, North. The integrated solutions will be offered to companies and institutions in finance, government and manufacturing, where data security and regulatory compliance are critical. results.title: Wartime Busan comes back into focus through soldiers' lenses
results.content: During the 1950-53 Korean War, as North Korean forces swept down the peninsula and Seoul fell twice, this southeastern port city became Korea’s wartime capital — a crowded, improvised refuge filled with displaced families, foreign troops and mountains of military supplies. Now, a new exhibition offers a rare glimpse of that turbulent era not through official state archives, but through the personal cameras of foreign soldiers who served there. Opening Nov. 24 at the Busan Citizens Park History Hall, “Records of War Veterans, 1950s Busan Captured on Camera” brings together photographs taken by unnamed soldiers who documented the city’s wartime transformation and everyday resilience. The free exhibition, organized by the Provisional Capital Memorial Hall under the Busan Modern and Contemporary History Museum, runs through May 30, 2027. results.title: St. Josephine Bakhita
results.content: One of the five symbolic patron saints of World Youth Day Seoul 2027 is St. Josephine Bakhita, a former slave who became a religious sister and a witness to hope, freedom, forgiveness and faith transformed through suffering. As the resolution of the 12th General Chapter of our Congregation is concerned with “safeguarding,” the presence of St. Josephine Bakhita among the list of saints drew my attention. Josephine Bakhita was born in Darfur, Sudan, around 1869. After being kidnapped at age seven and sold into slavery, she suffered intensely. She was even stripped of her own name and given the ironic name “Bakhita,” meaning “fortunate or the lucky one,” by her captors. She forgot her own name from the overwhelming shock and fear of her experiences. She spent years being treated as property. results.content: A KFC restaurant near Konkuk University Station in Seoul reopens Tuesday as a hero-themed restaurant inspired by Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Doomsday,” which is set to hit local theaters on Dec. 16. The promotion runs through Dec. 27, as KFC Korea collaborates with Marvel Studios to transform selected outlets with interiors inspired by the latest installment in the blockbuster franchise. results.title: Korean workers embrace AI, but productivity gains remain elusive: BOK
results.content: Korean workers are saving time by using artificial intelligence (AI), but the technology has yet to deliver meaningful productivity gains in the workplace, a Bank of Korea (BOK) report showed Tuesday. The share of workers using generative AI for work rose to 66.5 percent this year, up from 51.8 percent in 2025, according to the central bank's report on AI use and productivity. The survey covered 16,342 employed people aged 18 to 64 between August and September. The growing use of AI has helped workers save time while performing their tasks. Based on a 40-hour workweek, workers who used AI for work saved an average of 9.2 percent of their working time, or about 3.7 hours a week. That was more than double the 3.8 percent, equivalent to 1.5 hours, reported a year earlier. But the time saved has not necessarily translated into higher output or better quality work. results.title: Fear of wearable devices spreads beyond education sector
results.content: Smart glasses — once seen mainly as a new consumer gadget — are now being treated as a mounting security threat in Korea, with the military and major tech firms tightening restrictions on artificial intelligence (AI)-powered wearables. The latest measures come after AI smart devices emerged as a new tool for cheating on exams, after a top scorer in this year’s tax accountant exam admitted to cheating with the help of a miniature camera and a smarphone. This has sparked concerns that such devices could be used to secretly record military facilities or steal corporate secrets. The issue has prompted major Korean companies to tighten restrictions on AI wearables at their facilities. Samsung Electronics, which prohibits unauthorized photography using smart devices, requires smart glasses brought onto company premises to have stickers covering their cameras. results.content: As concerns grow over the working conditions of teenage K-pop idols after an article on the topic in the New York Times early this month, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Tuesday that it will look into how well the basic rights of underage entertainers are protected next year. The move comes amid mounting scrutiny of the industry following a Nov. 5 report by The New York Times, which found that the contract girl group NewJeans signed as minors omitted key protections for underage performers. “We plan to conduct a fact-finding survey on the status of underage entertainers in 2027, but its timing, scope and methods have yet to be decided,” Choi Hye-ji, a public relations officer at the ministry, told The Korea Times. results.title: Technical hurdles complicate efforts to curb AI cheating
results.content: Korea is on high alert as cases of cheating using smart glasses and other artificial intelligence (AI)-powered devices unnerve students ahead of this year’s College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday. However, technical hurdles are complicating efforts to prevent such devices from being used during the exam. The government is considering whether to disable public Wi-Fi services at all test sites during the exam, although questions remain over the effectiveness of such a measure. Most commercially available smart glasses require a separate internet connection to access AI features. As long as a paired smartphone has access to a mobile network, the glasses can continue to use AI functions without a Wi-Fi connection. results.title: Seoul expands job opportunities for foreign talent with 117 employers at career fair
results.content: Seoul is stepping up efforts to turn its growing international student population into a global workforce, bringing 117 companies and institutions together Wednesday for a career fair aimed at helping foreign residents find jobs and build lives in Korea. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said the 2026 Seoul Foreign Job Fair will be held at SETEC in Gangnam District, with more than 2,500 foreign job seekers registered in advance, underscoring strong interest from international talent and local employers. Organized under the theme “Global Talent, Greater Seoul,” the second annual event is expected to attract more than 3,000 international students and foreign nationals seeking employment in Korea. results.title: Seoul drone light show draws 240,000 visitors, puts city on global stage
results.content: Seoul’s night sky became an international attraction this year, as its Han River drone light shows drew more than 240,000 visitors and turned viral footage of Marvel characters into a global showcase for the city. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that eight performances held between April and October at Yeouido, Ttukseom and Jamsil Hangang parks attracted a combined 240,782 people, averaging 30,098 visitors per show. The attendance represented a 7.2 percent increase from 2025 and was 2.7 times the figure recorded during the event’s inaugural year in 2023. Foreign visitors accounted for 62,555 attendees, or 26 percent of the total. At the April 10 performance featuring BT21 characters at Yeouido Hangang Park, international visitors made up nearly half the audience, at 49.6 percent. results.title: Sejong University ranks No. 1 in Korea for top 10% most-cited papers
results.content: Sejong University ranked No. 1 in Korea for the share of its papers among the world’s top 10 percent most-cited publications in the 2026 CWTS Leiden Ranking Open Edition. The university said it has topped the domestic rankings for four consecutive years since the revised edition was introduced in 2023, underscoring its research strength. Under the fractional counting method, which allocates credit among co-authors according to their respective contributions, 14.4 percent of the university’s publications ranked among the world’s top 10 percent most-cited papers, placing Sejong 157th globally and 81st in Asia. The indicator, compiled by the Centre for Science and Technology Studies (CWTS) at Leiden University in the Netherlands, measures the proportion of a university’s publications that rank among the top 10 percent most-cited papers in their respective fields and publication years. results.content: The leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) said Tuesday that the party will push for legislation to bar those caught using artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on national exams from retaking the tests, including the annual college entrance exam, for up to 10 years. Rep. Kim Min-seok's remarks came after the top scorer on the country's national tax accountant exam admitted to having used a microcamera and AI-assisted devices to cheat, raising concerns ahead of Thursday's nationwide college entrance exam. "We will prepare legislation to bar those caught cheating from taking the exam for up to 10 years," Kim said on the DPK's official YouTube channel. results.title: Alibaba.com wins customer trust award in Korea
results.content: Alibaba.com has won a customer trust award in Korea, as growing numbers of local businesses turn to the global sourcing platform to find overseas suppliers, manage payments and expand manufacturing partnerships. The global business-to-business commerce platform said Tuesday it received the top award in the business-to-business platform category at Forbes Korea's 2026 Customer Trust No. 1 Premium Brand awards, organized by JoongAng Ilbo and Forbes Korea. The recognition followed evaluations of brand competitiveness and reliability by consumers and experts, according to the company. Alibaba.com attributed the award to services designed to make international transactions safer and more efficient, including Trade Assurance, its transaction protection system, and Accio, its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered business assistant. results.title: Busan sees surge in repeat visitors from Taiwan
results.content: More than half of Taiwanese tourists visiting Busan are repeat travelers, underscoring the Korean port city’s growing appeal beyond first-time sightseers, according to a survey by municipal tourism officials. The Busan Metropolitan Government and Busan Tourism Organization said Monday that their promotional campaign at the 2026 Taiwan International Travel Fair, held Nov. 6-9 at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, attracted more than 8,000 visitors. Of the 4,987 people surveyed at the booth, 55.3 percent said they had previously visited Busan, while 23 percent had returned at least twice. Interest in future travel was even stronger, with 90.1 percent saying they intended to visit or return to Busan within the next year. results.title: CJ CheilJedang introduces biodegradable pellets for artificial sports turf
results.content: CJ CheilJedang, Korea’s largest food and biotechnology company, introduced biodegradable artificial turf pellets made from plant-based materials at a Korean sports facility for the first time, marking a step toward reducing microplastic pollution on playing fields. The company said Tuesday it had completed installation of polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA)-based infill at Korea Football Park Stadium in Cheonan, South Chungcheong Province, which houses training facilities for Korea's national soccer teams. Artificial turf infill helps support synthetic grass and absorb impact, reducing the risk of injuries among players, but conventional products are largely made from petroleum-based synthetic rubber. results.title: Cabinet passes motion to promulgate bill mandating special counsel probe into alleged fabricated indictments
results.content: The Cabinet on Tuesday passed a motion to promulgate a parliament-approved bill mandating a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the preceding administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. The Cabinet meeting was presided over by Prime Minister Han Seong-sook as Lee was away for annual regional summits. The bill, which the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)-controlled National Assembly approved earlier this month, takes effect upon publication in the official gazette. The legislation calls for appointing an independent counsel to investigate suspicions that the prosecution under the former Yoon Suk Yeol administration had fabricated evidence or induced false statements to build cases against then opposition leader Lee and others. results.title: Korean edtech startup sees AI transform how students are assessed
results.content: Teachers are spending increasing amounts of time grading assignments and handling administrative work, leaving less time for students, but a Korean education technology startup believes artificial intelligence (AI) can help change that equation. Hyperlearning, an AI-powered education technology company specializing in assessment, is developing tools that automate grading, generate examination questions and provide personalized feedback, with ambitions to expand from Korea into Southeast Asia and the United States. Its co-founder and CEO Lim Chae-won believes AI should do more than make existing assessment methods faster. results.title: Korea to ground flights for 35 minutes during CSAT English test Thursday
results.content: Korea will suspend aircraft takeoffs nationwide for 35 minutes Thursday as students sit for the English listening section of the annual college entrance exam, with 130 flights facing schedule changes. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said Tuesday that aircraft will be prohibited from taking off between 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m., when the listening test for the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) will be administered. The measure is intended to eliminate aircraft noise that could interfere with students' concentration during one of the exam's most closely monitored sections. Aircraft already in the air will be required to remain at least 3 kilometers above ground during the restricted period. Emergency and other urgent flights will be exempt. results.content: Veteran Korean actress Lee Young-ae, 55, is drawing attention for her seemingly ageless appearance after sharing photos of herself alongside K-pop girl group aespa at the 2026 Melon Music Awards (MMA). results.title: Complaint filed against education minister for dereliction of duty over AI cheating
results.content: A former Seoul city councilor filed a complaint against Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin on Tuesday, accusing him of dereliction of duty after the minister said it would be difficult to catch all forms of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI). Lee Jong-bae, a former Seoul city council member from the main opposition People Power Party, said he submitted the complaint to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency over the remarks Choi made during a plenary session of the National Assembly's education committee the previous day when questioned about AI-assisted cheating. The move came amid heightened public anxiety over such misconduct ahead of Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an annual national college entrance exam, known as Suneung in Korean. results.title: Korea regains top spot in global OLED shipments in H1
results.content: Korea regained the top spot in the global organic light-emitting diode (OLED) market by shipment volume in the first half of this year, overtaking China for the first time in two years, industry data showed Tuesday. Korea accounted for 50.1 percent of global OLED shipments in the first half, narrowly surpassing China's 49.8 percent, according to data compiled by the Korea Display Industry Association (KDIA). In terms of revenue, Korea's share of the global OLED market rose 3 percentage points on-year to 68.3 percent, while China's market share fell to 31.7 percent from 34.5 percent a year earlier. Korea's revenue-based market share increased for the third consecutive year, following 64.2 percent in 2024 and 65.3 percent in 2025.

results.title: Sejong Center's outdoor garden transforms into winter market
results.content: A popular garden in central Seoul is trading autumn jazz for Christmas lights, hot snacks and handmade gifts. Sejong Center for the Performing Arts said Tuesday that Curtain Call Garden will reopen as a winter market from Tuesday through Jan. 3 in its Art Garden courtyard, operating daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. The seasonal transformation will bring traditional winter treats, warm drinks, crafts and holiday decorations to the space, which opened in October as part of Seoul's initiative to stimulate nighttime economic activity. Visitors can buy fish-shaped pastries, caramel-filled fried doughnuts, roasted sweet potatoes and savory fish cake from Happy Carp Bread, while Tea Tree Vin Chaud will serve warm mulled wine and highballs. results.title: 2026 Korea Times Forum
results.content: The Korea Times will host a forum titled "Capital market advancement: Giant leap toward era of Korea premium" on Nov. 24. The event will take place from 9 a.m. to 11:50 a.m. at the Grand Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in central Seoul. Korea's capital market stands at a pivotal moment as it moves beyond the "Korea discount" toward an era of "Korea premium." While government-led reforms and the artificial intelligence boom have laid the groundwork for this transition, strengthening global competitiveness and investor confidence remains a key challenge. Bringing together policymakers, financial market experts and business leaders from Korea and abroad, the forum will serve as a platform to exchange insights and explore strategies for the future of Korea's capital market. results.title: Min Hee-jin denies influencing NewJeans' contract termination after police refer breach of trust case to prosecutors
results.content: Former ADOR CEO Min Hee-jin has denied allegations that she influenced K-pop girl group NewJeans to terminate its exclusive contract with the agency, after police referred her to prosecutors on suspicion of breach of trust. Ooak Records, the agency currently headed by Min, said in an official statement Monday that Min had played no role in prompting the group's decision to end its contract with ADOR. "Min did not exercise any influence whatsoever to induce NewJeans to decide to terminate its contract," the company said. Min's side pointed to an earlier decision by Seoul's Yongsan Police Station not to refer a separate case involving allegations of occupational breach of trust and an attempted takeover of management control to prosecutors. results.title: Lee urges stronger ASEAN+3 role as regional shocks spread
results.content: MANILA — President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday urged ASEAN Plus Three, a regional cooperation framework comprising the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) plus Korea, China and Japan, to strengthen its role in tackling shared crises as conflicts and economic shocks increasingly spill across borders. Speaking at the ASEAN Plus Three summit, held alongside the 2026 ASEAN Summit and related gatherings in Manila, Lee noted that the first gathering of Korean, Chinese and Japanese leaders in the capital of the Philippines in 1999 served as a model for overcoming differences through common economic interests, urging today’s leaders to draw lessons from their predecessors’ decision to open a new chapter of cooperation. “Today, we face international conditions and an economic environment that are far more complex and uncertain than when ASEAN Plus Three was launched,” Lee said.

results.title: Sungkyunkwan University holds global living lab on AI-driven traffic solutions
results.content: Sungkyunkwan University held the final presentation session of a global living lab project at its Seoul campus on Nov. 5, showcasing student-led efforts to address urban transportation challenges using artificial intelligence (AI) and geospatial technologies. Organized by the university’s ANCHOR Project Group in collaboration with Jeonbuk National University, the second Global Livinglab: AI×Traffic System aimed to help students tackle real-world urban problems through interdisciplinary research and practical problem-solving. The initiative also sought to nurture industry-ready talent in the future mobility sector by combining universities’ educational and research capabilities with the expertise of public institutions and industry partners. results.title: Top scorer of tax accountant exam apologizes for cheating before police questioning
results.content: The top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam apologized Tuesday for cheating on the test as he appeared before police to undergo questioning. The man, surnamed Han, admitted Sunday to using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative artificial intelligence (AI) to score top marks on the exam, sparking public outcry and concerns over cheating in national exams. "I am truly sorry to those who prepared for the exam and those involved," he told reporters at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's office in western Seoul. "I will not hide what I did and will tell the truth to investigative authorities." He said he would take responsibility for his actions but did not answer questions about whether he acted alone and how he prepared the equipment to cheat on the test.
